title: Vietoris wins a wet Oschersleben lottery for Mercedes
dek: Christian Vietoris won a wet, three-safety-car Oschersleben race for HWA Mercedes from 16th on the grid by 0.674 seconds, after pole-sitter Marco Wittmann dropped to 19th and Jamie Green's lead evaporated.

chapters.title: Wittmann leads, Mercedes need a change
text: The DTM returned two weeks after the Hockenheim opener to the Motorsport Arena Oschersleben on 18 May. Marco Wittmann arrived as the points leader after winning the first race for BMW Team RMG, with Mattias Ekström and Adrien Tambay on the podium and Rockenfeller fourth. Mercedes-Benz had left Hockenheim without a point, its best finisher 11th. The performance weights had been adjusted since: Wittmann and Bruno Spengler both spoke of five additional kilograms in their BMWs, a sign of the first-race result.
This was the second of the ten races and, as at Hockenheim, the weekend was a single Sunday race with a 75-minute limit.

chapters.title: Molina's pole is taken away and Wittmann inherits it
text: Miguel Molina looked to have the pole position. The Audi driver went fastest in the first session, second in the second, and then set 1:20.007 in the final one, 0.509 seconds clear of Wittmann's 1:20.516. A post-qualifying check changed that: the rear-wing endplates on his Audi stuck out 2.7 and 1.5 millimetres beyond what the technical regulations allow. The stewards excluded him, Abt chose not to appeal, and Molina started the race from 23rd and last.

That promoted Wittmann to pole, just ahead of Tambay, whose 1:20.519 was only 0.003 seconds slower, and António Félix da Costa, who showed his Hockenheim pace was no fluke in the third-placed MTEK BMW (1:20.582). Scheider and Rockenfeller were fourth and fifth in the Phoenix Audis, Spengler sixth and Mortara seventh. Farfus, ninth fastest, narrowly missed the final session and started eighth after the reshuffle.

Mercedes-Benz again struggled. Wehrlein, ninth on the grid, was the best by a distance, while Vietoris and Gary Paffett were 16th and 17th. Wickens, di Resta, Daniel Juncadella and Petrov were 19th to 22nd after being eliminated in the first session, as was Timo Glock, whose BMW had a power-steering problem and who missed the second session by 0.019 seconds.

chapters.title: Rain on the grid, Vietoris pits at once
text: Rain started falling on the formation lap and the grid was split by tyre choice. Vietoris and Juncadella, starting from the back half, came into the pits straight after it to change to rain tyres, a move that looked like a mistake on a track that had not yet become wet. Wittmann kept the lead at the start from a well-placed Scheider and Tambay, with Félix da Costa behind them.

Molina, from the back of the grid, was 11th by lap three and ninth by lap eight. As the rain strengthened, the drivers on standard tyres lost places lap by lap, and the stops began. Pascal Wehrlein hit the rear of Edoardo Mortara's Audi and spun him, and received a five-second pit-stop penalty. Rockenfeller, who had started fifth on standard tyres and fallen as far as 19th, was called in for rain tyres on lap eight. That early call turned out to be the right one.

chapters.title: Three neutralisations reshuffle the order
text: After the early stops, Wickens went into the gravel after contact with Molina's Audi near the pit exit, and the first safety car came out. It caught Paffett, who was the last runner on slick tyres, at the head of the field. On the restart Wittmann ran wide into the gravel at the first corner trying to pass him and lost the lead to Tambay, and a few corners later Glock's BMW hit Rockenfeller and was left in the gravel. Farfus took a five-second penalty for an unsafe release in the pit lane, and the second safety car followed.

After that restart Jamie Green, who had started tenth, passed first Scheider and then Tambay and took the lead, building a lead of more than ten seconds. It was wiped out when Wehrlein stopped in the gravel and brought out the third safety car, which closed the field up again. The race then ran to its maximum time of 75 minutes instead of to a set number of laps.

chapters.title: Slicks cost Green the lead
text: The drivers who had made their mandatory stop early, such as Rockenfeller and Mortara, now had the advantage, because they would not have to lose time in the pits again. Green still had to stop and took a gamble on slicks as the track dried, and he dropped to eighth with around eight minutes left. Vietoris, who had changed tyres after the formation lap and had stopped once more, moved forward as the others came in: he overtook Rockenfeller for 13th, then Mortara for eighth, and was in the lead shortly before the end.

chapters.title: Vietoris wins by 0.674 seconds
text: Vietoris took his first DTM win after 44 laps in 1:15:28.785, 0.674 seconds ahead of Rockenfeller, who closed in again towards the end without getting close enough to pass. Mortara was third, 7.769 seconds behind, and di Resta fourth, 8.906 seconds back. Farfus took fifth, the best BMW, 9.326 seconds back, having said that without the five-second penalty he might have been third. Molina climbed from last to sixth and set the fastest lap, a 1:23.597 on lap five.

Scheider was seventh and Paffett eighth, ahead of Tomczyk and Tambay, who had led after the first restart and finished tenth. Green slid off on the last lap and was classified 18th, one lap down, while Wittmann, who had led the opening laps, finished 19th, also a lap down, after the restart error and a technical problem. Wehrlein, Juncadella, Glock and Wickens did not finish.

chapters.title: A maiden win for Vietoris and the points lead for Rockenfeller
text: Vietoris called it his first DTM victory and said that Mercedes had hoped for rain because its dry pace was not good enough, and that the team had worked out a perfect strategy. Mercedes-Benz's head of DTM management Wolfgang Schattling said the crew's decision in a tricky phase of the race was the key and that, before the start, no one had expected a win, warning that the car was still behind in normal conditions. It was Mercedes-Benz's first points of the season after a blank at Hockenheim, with Vietoris having gained 15 places from his grid slot and di Resta finishing fourth, just short of the podium, even after he felt his race was over when he was pushed off the track. Paffett was eighth and said he was annoyed with himself for an early spin.

Rockenfeller, second, took the lead of the championship. He called it "a chaotic race", said that starting on standard tyres had been the wrong choice for the conditions and that the team had made a superb decision to call him in at the right moment. Audi head of DTM Dieter Gass said it was a bit disappointing after Audi had led with three cars and a ten-second margin. Green, who lost the lead, said he had put too much pressure on Molina in the chicane and lost the rear. Mortara, who took third after being spun early, said the inflation pressure on his second set of rain tyres had been very low at first, while Molina's sixth place and fastest lap from the back of the grid confirmed his Saturday pace. Audi reported 65,000 spectators over the weekend.

BMW had a poor day after the strong qualifying. Only Farfus and Martin Tomczyk scored, with Farfus fifth and Tomczyk ninth, and motorsport director Jens Marquardt said that luck had been missing from the pole position. Wittmann said he had braked too late at the restart while trying to pass Paffett and that his gears later stuck. Glock took responsibility for the contact with Rockenfeller and apologised, saying he had understeered and hit him.

In the championship Rockenfeller led with 30 points, ahead of Wittmann and Vietoris on 25, Ekström on 18, Tambay on 16 and Mortara on 15. The third race of the ten was due at the Hungaroring on 31 May and 1 June.

facts.v: Christian Vietoris won his first DTM race by 0.674 seconds after gaining 15 places from 16th on the grid.
